question: Within matched prior-trend/year weak and good exact-f696 126-session windows, does the frozen EMA/HOLD transform add enough cash to explain the observed weak-window cash proposal gap?

method.source: Only the bridge-pinned action inputs/raw_predictions frozen_current and inputs/source_targets frozen_current, f696 inputs/frame and exact original Stage1 0bp Tiered analysis/daily and rolling126 Recorder objects
method.identity: On all944 signal dates, accepted cash and other four outputs equal f696 proposal; source bridge identity result is verified before looking at weak/good intervals
method.daily_coordinate: raw cash, accepted cash, accepted-minus-raw cash; no account counterfactual
method.window_outcome: Exact f696 rolling126 paired log excess below/above zero, diagnostic only
method.matched_cell: Prior signal-day Qlib SOXX 5/20-session return-sign state x window first-trade year; keep cells containing both outcomes and weight by the smaller group count
method.coverage: All944 days, 16 source quarters, 819 overlapping126-session windows; preserve2023/2026 partial endpoints and report 2023 unmatched state-year cells
method.measure: Weak-minus-good mean raw cash, accepted cash, and accepted-minus-raw cash, per matched cell and pooled descriptive weighting; report annual mean delta and sign counts
method.stop: Stop if source hashes/NAS, 944/819 coverage, Qlib calendar or exact target/f696 identity fail. Do not infer that replacing EMA/HOLD produces the frozen-path component return or full account value.

scientific_boundary: Postmodel coordinate differences and outcome-defined overlapping windows do not certify a tradable switch or causal performance gain. A changed transform would need a separately frozen full own-state 0bp Tiered account and all SOXX gates.
